reason: The cited evidence shows that SRO increases strength in the CoCrNi ternary (E2) and that nanotwins are observed in both ternary and quinary alloys (E1), but neither passage provides evidence that SRO is higher in the reduced-complexity alloys compared to the quinary alloy, nor that SRO promotes twin nucleation. The key premise of differential SRO between alloy complexities is unsupported.
premises: Reduced-complexity alloys (ternary/quaternary) exhibit higher SRO than the quinary alloy
Higher SRO enhances dislocation pinning and promotes deformation twin nucleation
Enhanced SRO and twinning lead to higher yield strength and work-hardening rate
The quinary alloy has a more random atomic arrangement that diminishes SRO effects
